title: Finite morphisms preserve closed nowhere dense subsets
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $T\subseteq|Y|$ be closed and nowhere dense, meaning that the interior of its closure in $|Y|$ is empty. Then $f(T)\subseteq|X|$ is closed and nowhere dense. No surjectivity, reducedness, integrality, Noetherianity or flatness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $f(T)$ is closed. Choose an affine open cover $X=\bigcup V_\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a) the restriction $f^{-1}(V_\alpha)\to V_\alpha$ is finite. The subset $T\cap f^{-1}(V_\alpha)$ is closed in this open subspace and has empty interior: any open contained in it would also be open in $Y$ and contained in $T$. Its image is $f(T)\cap V_\alpha$. It therefore suffices to prove the result for affine $X$.

source.place: Tag 03HX, first paragraph; Tag 03HP local assertion expanded directly.

proof.text: Assume $X$ affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-section-cover]: write $b:X\prime\to X$ for its surjective finite locally free cover, $a:Y\prime=Y\times_X X\prime\to Y$ for the other projection, and $f\prime:Y\prime\to X\prime$ for the base-changed map. It gives a closed immersion $j:Y\prime\hookrightarrow W$ and a finite locally free $q:W\to X\prime$ with $qj=f\prime$, where finitely many closed subschemes of $W$ cover it and each maps isomorphically to $X\prime$.

Finite locally free means finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; thus $a$ and $b$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Put $T\prime=a^{-1}(T)$. It is closed by continuity. If an open $O\subseteq Y\prime$ lies in $T\prime$, its open image $a(O)$ lies in $T$, so $O=\varnothing$. Hence $T\prime$ is nowhere dense (Tag 03HR). A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $A=j(T\prime)$ is closed in $W$; any open of $W$ contained in $A$ has empty inverse image under $j$, hence is empty itself. Thus $A$ is nowhere dense (Tag 03HQ).

source.place: Tag 03HX, second paragraph; Topology Tags 03HR and 03HQ, with their elementary arguments written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nowhere-dense-section-cover-image] to $q:W\to X\prime$, its finite closed section cover from step 2, and the closed nowhere dense $A$ of step 3. It gives that $q(A)=f\prime(T\prime)$ is closed and nowhere dense in $X\prime$.

source.place: Tag 03HX, final paragraph (finite closed section-cover case).

proof.text: The actual scheme-point identity [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], applied to $Y\prime=Y\times_X X\prime$ and $T\subseteq|Y|$, gives $f\prime(T\prime)=b^{-1}(f(T))$. If $U\subseteq X$ is open and contained in $f(T)$, then $b^{-1}(U)$ is open and contained in this nowhere dense set, hence empty. Surjectivity of $b$ gives $U=\varnothing$. Since $f(T)$ is closed, this proves it is nowhere dense on the affine base.

source.place: Tag 03HX, second paragraph, displayed image equality and descent through b; Topology Tag 03HR.

proof.text: Return to the original affine cover. Step 5 applied to each restriction of step 1 shows that $f(T)\cap V_\alpha$ has empty interior in $V_\alpha$. Any open $U\subseteq X$ contained in $f(T)$ has $U\cap V_\alpha=\varnothing$ for every $\alpha$, hence $U=\varnothing$. Together with closedness from step 1 this is exactly the desired closed nowhere dense conclusion. The argument also covers an empty source or empty target.
